transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I Corva Coleman, the president of Iran says his country
is still ready to follow through with a proposed seven-day plan that it presented to the U.S.
It's aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
NPR's Hadil Al-Shelchi reports President Trump rejected the proposal on Saturday.
In an interview with CBS's Face the Nation that aired on Sunday, Masoud Pezashqyan said
that after the seven-day milestone, and once mutual blockades are lifted, Iran was willing
to sit down for broader talks to formally end military conflict and address its nuclear
program.
In the interview, Pezashqyan said that Iran does not seek to develop nuclear weapons and
defended its civilian nuclear program.
Pezashqyan also addressed the lack of public appearances by the new supreme leader following
U.S.-Israeli strikes that killed his father.
The Iranian president said he had met the new leader twice and that he was healthy.
President Trump said on Saturday that he rejected Iran's seven-day proposal, but that he was
still open to negotiating.
Hadil Al-Shelchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
The U.S. ambassador to China says President Trump remains a strong supporter of Taiwan.
David Perdue spoke after Trump met China's president last week.
Perdue told Fox News Sunday Trump is approving weapons sales to Taiwan, but Perdue also had
another startling comment.
President Trump's already approved in 11 billion.
There are continuing conversations about other sales.
He and President Xi talk about that every time they get together.
But President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world.
He actually asked President Xi would he like to buy some at one point.
But other news organizations, including the New York Times, report the White House denies
there are any plans for the Trump administration to sell weapons to China.
They report it's illegal for the U.S. to sell arms to China.
Fox opened lower this morning as chipmaker Nvidia announces a massive stock buyback plan.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average slid about 240 points in
early trading.
Nvidia stock has jumped more than fivefold over the last year as the company profits
from the artificial intelligence boom.
But CEO Jensen Wong still thinks the shares are undervalued.
The company's increased its share buyback authorization by a whopping $150 billion.
Diesel prices rose after President Trump rejected a proposal from Iran to reopen the Strait
of Hormuz.
AAA says retail gasoline prices in the U.S. are hovering around $4.47 a gallon.
Diesel prices have dipped just slightly to an average of $6.45.
The Trump administration wants to allow cars to burn more gasoline.
The administration is releasing new fuel economy standards today that would allow cars to be
31 percent less efficient in the next five years.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Speaker Nvidia has also announced it's releasing a new software platform.
It is aimed at stopping rogue AI agents from acting without human oversight.
You're listening to NPR.
Authorities in the U.K. say they have foiled an attempted terror plot near an airbase in
western England.
After getting a tip, authorities stop three vehicles to search them and say they have
arrested five British nationals in connection with the suspected plot.
The U.S. government uses the U.K. airbase to launch some of its military attacks on
Iran.
A nor'easter soaked coastal communities along the east coast all weekend.
The storm is weakening, but flooding is a problem.
David Wright from Ocean State Media reports one death is being connected to the storm.
The nor'easter walloped the region with heavy rains and winds clocked as high as 70 miles
per hour in New York City.
One Brooklyn man who worked for the city housing authority was struck and killed by a falling
tree.
In some towns on the Jersey shore, the water was waist deep.
At the height of the storm, 180,000 customers in New Jersey alone lost power.
Work crews were busy all weekend long, and most of the outages have been restored.
On Nantucket, the storm deposited a huge chunk of a shipwreck onto the beach.
It may be part of a three-masted schooner that sank in 1884.
For NPR News, I'm David Wright in Greenport, New York.
Unionized musicians from the Cleveland Orchestra ended their strike.
They have agreed to a new three-year contract.
The musicians say they won a fair compensation package.
The Cleveland Orchestra's president says the deal was driven by good faith negotiation.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Iranian President Pezashqyan says Iran still ready to pursue seven-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz
U.S. Ambassador Perdue says Trump remains strong supporter of Taiwan, approving weapons sales
Nvidia announces massive $150 billion stock buyback plan as shares jump over past year
Diesel prices rise after Trump rejects Iran's proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
Trump administration releases new fuel economy standards allowing cars 31 percent less efficiency
Nvidia releases new software platform aimed at stopping rogue AI agents from acting unsupervised
U.K. authorities foil suspected terror plot near airbase, arrest five British nationals
Nor'easter weakens after soaking East Coast with heavy rain, winds, one death reported
Nor'easter causes waist-deep flooding in Jersey Shore towns, 180,000 lose power in New Jersey
Storm deposits huge chunk of 1884 shipwreck onto Nantucket beach
Unionized musicians from Cleveland Orchestra end strike, agree to new three-year contract
